title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: Student (EE1) shares their personal identity (student id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) during the login and submission process. This is a low-severity threat as the data is shared for a legitimate purpose (coursework), but it exposes the student's identity to the system.
assumptions: The student is authenticated and the submission is authorized.

title: Student Data Processing
description: Student (EE1) shares their personal data (student id, work file, course) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1). This is a medium-severity threat as the data is processed and stored by the system, potentially allowing for unauthorized access or misuse.
assumptions: The student has the right to submit the work file and the course.

title: Portal Data Processing
description: Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives and processes student data (student id, work file, course, submission timestamp). This is a medium-severity threat as the system processes sensitive personal information, which could be used for identification or further data aggregation.
assumptions: The portal has appropriate security controls in place.

title: Identification of Student
description: The source element (P1) shares data containing a unique identifier (student id) for the requesting role. This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) because the data contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, which can be used to link or identify the user.
assumptions: The data in the submission request includes a student id field.

title: Identification of Course
description: The source element (P1) shares data containing a unique identifier (course) for the requesting role. This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) because the data contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (the course entity), which can be used to link or identify the user.
assumptions: The data in the submission request includes a course field.

title: Identification of File Reference
description: The source element (P1) shares data containing a unique identifier (file reference) for the requesting role. This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) because the data contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (the file entity), which can be used to link or identify the user.
assumptions: The data in the submission request includes a file reference field.

title: Identification of Requesting Role
description: The source element (P1) shares data containing a unique identifier (requesting role) for the requesting role. This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) because the data contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (the requesting role), which can be used to link or identify the user.
assumptions: The data in the submission request includes a requesting role field.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The assignment file (containing student id, course, and submission time) is explicitly shared from the Process (P2) to the DataStore (DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system transfers personal data across a boundary to a known third party (the store).
assumptions: The assignment file contains personal data (student id) that is being transferred.

title: Data Disclosure in Transit
description: The assignment file is transmitted via the data flow (DF3) to the DataStore. The transmission itself exposes the data to potential interception or metadata-based identification, constituting a data-centric threat.
assumptions: The assignment file is transmitted over a network.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The DataStore (DS1) receives the assignment file and stores it. Storing the data constitutes a data disclosure as the system transfers the data to a known location for processing.
assumptions: The assignment file is stored in the DataStore.

title: Teacher's Request for Submission Queue
description: The Teacher (ExternalEntity) initiates a request to the Grades Portal Web App (Process) to retrieve the queue of submissions for their courses. This action triggers the identification of the specific data set (the queue) that the Teacher is authorized to access.
assumptions: The Teacher has the necessary permissions to request this data.

title: Data in Transit: Teacher-Portal Linkage
description: The data flow carries the Teacher's identity and the specific course identifiers associated with the requested queue. This meta-data allows the Portal to potentially link or identify the Teacher with the specific data set they are requesting, creating a potential privacy risk.
assumptions: The data in transit is not encrypted or anonymized.

title: Portal Processing of Requested Data
description: The Grades Portal Web App (Process) receives the Teacher's request and processes it by retrieving the submission queue. This processing action may involve storing the Teacher's identity and course context in a way that creates a privacy risk.
assumptions: The Portal processes the request without additional safeguards.

title: Student Data Exposure
description: The process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) shares student names, work content, and submission times with the external entity EE3 (Teacher). This interaction is valid under the mapping table (Process->ExternalEntity), but the act of sharing sensitive student data with an external party introduces a privacy risk. The threat arises at the source element (S) because the process's act of sharing causes the exposure of the data.
assumptions: The portal is configured to share all submissions to the teacher.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow DF5 transmits student names, work content, and submission times between the portal and the teacher. The threat arises at the data flow (fl) because the data-centric threat involves meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them. The teacher's identity and the student's identity are linked via the data in transit, creating a potential for data-centric privacy threats.
assumptions: The portal and teacher exchange data via the standard web interface.

title: Teacher Data Processing
description: The destination element (EE3, Teacher) receives the student data and processes or stores it. The threat arises at the destination (D) because the teacher's act of receiving and processing student names, work content, and submission times may lead to unauthorized access, storage, or misuse of this sensitive information.
assumptions: The teacher's system is configured to store and process all submissions.

title: Teacher Identity Disclosure
description: Teacher (EE3) shares their identity (grader id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to record a grade. This is a valid interaction (Process->Process) and the threat arises at the source element where the act of sharing causes the threat.

title: Teacher Feedback Disclosure
description: Teacher (EE3) shares written feedback text with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to record a grade. This is a valid interaction (Process->Process) and the threat arises at the source element where the act of sharing causes the threat.

title: Data Processing for Student Identification
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the student id and grader id from the Teacher (EE3) and processes/store them. This is a valid interaction (Process->Process) and the threat arises at the destination element where the recipient processes/store data in a way that causes the threat.

title: Student Identification
description: The source element (Process P2) shares student identification data (student id) with the destination element (DataStore DS2). This creates a privacy threat where the student's identity is exposed in transit or at the destination, potentially allowing for unauthorized linkage or identification of the student.

title: Course Identification
description: The source element (Process P2) shares course identification data (course) with the destination element (DataStore DS2). This creates a privacy threat where the course's identity is exposed, potentially allowing for unauthorized linkage or identification of the course.

title: Feedback Data Exposure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares feedback data (feedback) with the destination element (DataStore DS2). This creates a privacy threat where the feedback content is exposed, potentially allowing for unauthorized access or misuse of the feedback.

title: Grader Identity Exposure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares grader identity data (grader id) with the destination element (DataStore DS2). This creates a privacy threat where the grader's identity is exposed, potentially allowing for unauthorized linkage or identification of the grader.

title: Timestamp Exposure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares timestamp data (timestamp) with the destination element (DataStore DS2). This creates a privacy threat where the temporal context of the grade record is exposed, potentially allowing for unauthorized linkage or identification of the grade record.

title: Requesting Personal Data
description: The external entity (Student, EE1) requests its own personal data (grades and feedback) from the system. This action triggers an Identifying threat (I) because the system processes identified data, which can be used to link or identify the student.
assumptions: The student has the right to access their own grades and feedback.

title: Processing Personal Data
description: The process (Grades Portal Web App, P1) receives the student's request and processes the identified data (grades and feedback). This processing action can lead to a Data threat (D) if the data is stored or used in a way that compromises privacy.
assumptions: The process handles the data according to standard grading protocols.

title: Grade Data Exposure
description: The process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) shares its internal data (student grades) with an external entity (Student). This interaction is valid under the mapping table (Process->ExternalEntity), but the act of sharing sensitive personal data (grades) with an external party introduces a privacy risk. The threat arises at the source element (S) because the process's act of sharing causes the data to be exposed to the external entity.

title: Data Processing by External Entity
description: The external entity (Student, EE1) receives the grades data and processes it. The threat arises at the destination element (D) because the external entity may use the data for its own purposes (e.g., displaying grades, storing it, or using it for other analytics) without proper authorization or safeguards, which could lead to misuse or unauthorized access.

title: Identity Confusion
description: Parent (EE2) shares their identity with the system, which is then used to access the child's account. This creates a risk that the system cannot distinguish between the parent and the child, leading to unauthorized access to the child's data.
assumptions: The system treats the parent's login credentials as valid for the child's account.

title: Data Centric Threat: Identity Linking
description: The data flow transmits the parent's identity information (e.g., username, email, or session token) to the destination. This meta-data allows the system to link the parent's actions to the child's account, enabling the parent to access the child's private data.
assumptions: The system does not validate that the parent is the actual owner of the child's account.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The portal web app (P1) processes the parent's identity data to retrieve the child's grades. This processing action, without proper authorization or verification of the parent's identity, allows the system to access and potentially misuse the child's private educational data.
assumptions: The system has no mechanism to verify that the parent is authorized to access the child's account.

title: Grade Data Exposure
description: The process P1 shares sensitive student grades with the external entity EE2. This interaction is valid (Process->ExternalEntity) but the act of sharing causes a threat because the destination (EE2) may process or store this data in a way that causes a privacy threat, such as storing it in a way that allows identification or linkage.
assumptions: The parent entity (EE2) is an external system that may not have appropriate controls for storing or processing this data.

title: Data Linkage Risk
description: The data flow DF11 carries metadata about the parties involved (P1 and EE2). This meta-data could be used to link or identify the specific student records being shared, even if the data itself is encrypted.
assumptions: The metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them is not adequately protected.

title: Destination Processing Threat
description: The destination element EE2 receives the grades and feedback. The context suggests EE2 may process or store this data in a way that causes a threat, such as storing it in a way that allows identification or linkage.
assumptions: The parent entity (EE2) is an external system that may not have appropriate controls for storing or processing this data.

title: Unauthorized Account Creation
description: ExternalEntity EE4 (School Administrator) shares data (user credentials, parent-child relationships) with Process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) without explicit authorization or encryption, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive personal information.

title: Inappropriate Data Modification
description: EE4 modifies parent-child relationships (names, emails, roles) without verifying the integrity of the data or confirming the recipient's identity, potentially leading to data corruption or misuse.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: Process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) receives and processes sensitive data (parent-child relationships) without proper validation, potentially storing or using it for unauthorized purposes.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grading Service
description: The grading service (P2) writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory (DS3). If the service is not properly secured, an unauthorized user could access or modify these sensitive account records.

title: Data Modification by Grading Service
description: The grading service (P2) writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory (DS3). If the service is not properly secured, an unauthorized user could access or modify these sensitive account records.

title: Unauthorized Access to Account Directory
description: The account directory (DS3) receives data from the grading service (P2). If the directory is not properly secured, an unauthorized user could access or modify these sensitive account records.

title: Data Disclosure to External Entity
description: Process P2 (Assignment & Grading Service) shares full grade records, assignments, and account directory with external entity EE5 (Cloud Hosting Provider). This constitutes a data disclosure as the transfer of personal data across a boundary to a third party.
assumptions: The data transfer is intended and designed as part of the nightly backup and hosting replication process.

title: Data in Transit - Linking/Identification
description: Data-centric threat: The metadata associated with the data flow (e.g., source entity identifiers, destination entity identifiers, or data content itself) may be used to link or identify the parties involved in the transfer, potentially compromising privacy.
assumptions: The metadata used to identify the parties is not strictly required for the backup process but is present in transit.

title: Data Processing/Storage by External Entity
description: External entity EE5 receives and processes the data. The processing or storage of personal data by a third party may cause a threat, as the entity may use the data for its own purposes beyond the agreed scope.
assumptions: The external entity's processing activities are not strictly limited to the data transfer.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The data store (DS2) shares grade records with the assignment & grading service (P2). If the service has access to the data, it can potentially access or modify the records, leading to unauthorized access.

title: Data in Transit
description: Grade records are transmitted from the data store (DS2) to the assignment & grading service (P2). If the service has access to the data, it can potentially access or modify the records, leading to unauthorized access.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Grade Records
description: The assignment & grading service (P2) receives the grade records and may modify or access them in ways that are not authorized by the data store (DS2).
